meta.unit: The rise of the Gadianton band (Helaman 1–6)
principles: A people building with what the land lacks
A record naming its own limits
Peace with something growing inside it

world_behind.title: The chapter covers eleven years
world_behind.text: Verse 1 opens in the forty-third year and verse 37 closes in the fifty-third, with the contentions and the peace both measured by year.

world_behind.title: Contention drives the migration
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has an exceedingly great many leaving Zarahemla for the land northward in the same year as much contention and many dissensions.

world_behind.title: The land northward was stripped of timber
world_behind.text: Verses 5 and 6 say the desolation was a timber shortage left by earlier inhabitants, and that the destruction of that people gave the land its name. Alma 22:30 and 31 had said the same, and Ether 7:6 puts the Jaredite land of Moron next to it. The reader knows whose bones are meant.

world_behind.title: They build in cement and conserve trees
world_behind.text: Verse 7 has them expert in cement, verse 9 has saplings left to stand for future timber, and verse 10 has timber shipped north. Alma 50:2 to 6 describes Nephite building forty years earlier as banks of earth, timbers, and pickets; this is the record's only account of a change in construction technique.

world_behind.title: The people of Ammon go north too
world_behind.text: Verse 12 says many of the people of Ammon, Lamanites by birth, joined the migration north. Alma 27:26 had settled them in Jershon and Alma 35:13 had moved them to Melek for the war; this is their third relocation, and the record still calls them by birth rather than by residence.

world_behind.title: Mormon names his sources and their scale
world_behind.text: Verses 13 through 16 say many large records exist and that a hundredth part of the proceedings cannot fit in his work.

world_behind.title: The Gadianton combinations survive underground
world_behind.text: Verse 23 says they were established in the more settled parts and were not known to the heads of government, so they were not destroyed.

words.text: Wood cut for building. All five of the record's uses fall in this chapter, at verses 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10. The King James Bible uses it twenty-six times, mostly of Solomon's building projects (1 Kgs. 6–7).

A binding material for construction. All four of the record's uses are in this chapter, and the word appears nowhere in the King James Bible. Verse 7 credits the northern settlers with expertise in working it.
The carrying of goods by ship. The record uses the word twice, both in this chapter, and the King James Bible once, at John 6:24. Verse 10 has timber moved north by sea because the land had none.
Treated at Alma 17:14, of the Lamanites the sons of Mosiah went to teach. The record uses it six times. Verse 16 applies it to Nephites who have become Lamanites.
Cunning tricks meant to trap. The word occurs once in the record and twice in the King James Bible, including Ephesians 6:11, where the armor of God is put on to withstand them.
Being made holy. Both of the record's uses are in this verse, and the King James Bible has five. Verse 35 gives the cause as yielding the heart to God.

phrases.term: A little pride which was in the church
phrases.text: The first note of the chapter's theme, sounded in its quietest year. Verse 33 has the same word without the qualifier, and verse 36 has it growing daily.

phrases.term: They came to large bodies of water and many rivers
phrases.text: The record's description of how far north the migration reached. Mormon gives distance and water and no place names.

phrases.term: Because of the greatness of the destruction of the people who had before inhabited the land it was called desolate
phrases.text: The explanation of a name. Alma 22:30 had placed the land Desolation where a people had been destroyed, and this verse says the emptiness was a matter of timber.

phrases.term: Exceedingly expert in the working of cement
phrases.text: A people adapting to what the country lacks. The record has used "expert" of Zeezrom and of Gadianton, and uses it here of builders.

phrases.term: They did suffer whatsoever tree should spring up upon the face of the land that it should grow up
phrases.text: Deliberate conservation, stated as policy. The purpose given is timber for houses, cities, temples, synagogues, and sanctuaries in time to come.

phrases.term: A hundredth part of the proceedings of this people... cannot be contained in this work
phrases.text: Mormon's measure of what he has left out. Jacob 3:13 used the same fraction of an earlier generation.
The end of the line Mormon traces in a single verse: transgression, murder, plunder, scattering, and mixing until the name is gone. He writes it about his own people, from the far end.

phrases.term: Helaman did fill the judgment-seat with justice and equity
phrases.text: The verdict on a chief judge who held office through nine years of contention. Verse 37 gives his son Nephi the same sentence.

phrases.term: Which at that time were not known unto those who were at the head of government
phrases.text: The reason the combinations were not destroyed. Mormon attaches it to a year he calls continual peace.

phrases.term: Even the high priests and the teachers were themselves astonished beyond measure
phrases.text: The size of the growth surprised the people running the church. Verse 26 counts tens of thousands baptized.

phrases.term: Not into the church of God, but into the hearts of the people who professed to belong to the church of God
phrases.text: Mormon correcting his own phrase mid-sentence. The distinction places the fault in people rather than in the institution.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: The unit of the chapter is the calendar
verses.text: "The forty and" opens verses 1, 2, 3, 18, 19, 22, 23 and 32, and "the reign of the judges" anchors seven verses more. Ten years pass in thirty-seven verses, and the record keeps score by contention: a little pride in the forty-third, none in the forty-fourth, not much in the forty-fifth, much in the forty-sixth. Peace here is a quantity that gets measured annually rather than a condition.

verses.label: v. 5–7
verses.title: A building material explained by what is missing
verses.text: The land northward is not desolate, "save it were for timber," and the name is explained by something the record does not narrate: "the greatness of the destruction of the people who had before inhabited the land." Out of that absence comes the solution: "they did build houses of cement." The word appears three times in scripture, all of them in this chapter, and the record treats it as a technique the migrants had to become expert in.

verses.label: v. 13–16
verses.title: The refusal to write it all is itemized
verses.text: "A hundredth part of the proceedings of this people... cannot be contained in this work," and Mormon then lists fourteen kinds of thing he is leaving out, from shipbuilding to whoredoms. Verse 16 disposes of the fate of those other records without pausing for a full stop, ending "becoming Lamanites," and verse 17 returns him to his place: "And now I return again to mine account." The apology for brevity is the longest digression in the chapter.

verses.label: v. 23
verses.title: The peace has an exception the government cannot see
verses.text: "Continual peace established in the land, all save it were the secret combinations which Gadianton the robber had established in the more settled parts of the land, which at that time were not known unto those who were at the head of government." The record hands the reader a fact the rulers do not have, and states the consequence flatly: "therefore they were not destroyed out of the land."

verses.label: v. 27–29
verses.title: Three conclusions in a row, and the first one hedges
verses.text: Verse 27 opens "Thus we may see," a form used once in all of scripture. Verse 28 drops the modal to "thus we see," and verse 29 to "we see." The record grows more certain across three verses about mercy, an open gate, and a word that divides asunder, and it starts from the least confident of the three.

verses.label: v. 33
verses.title: The sentence stops to move the noun
verses.text: Pride "began to enter into the church" — and then the correction arrives inside the same verse, on a dash: "not into the church of God, but into the hearts of the people who professed to belong to the church of God." The record will not let the institution carry the fault, and repairs the attribution in front of the reader rather than rewriting the clause.

verses.label: v. 37
verses.title: Father and son get the same sentence
verses.text: Helaman filled the judgment-seat "with justice and equity" at verse 20; Nephi does it in identical words at verse 37, and the phrase occurs nowhere else in scripture. Both are said to walk in the ways of their father. The record hands the succession its verdict before the new judge has done anything, by copying out the old one.

chapter.title: Migration is reported as a symptom
chapter.text: Verse 3 puts the departure in the same sentence as much contention and many dissensions. The record does not present the move north as opportunity alone.

chapter.title: A shortage produces a technology
chapter.text: Verses 7 through 11 have a people without timber becoming expert in cement, conserving trees, and importing wood by sea. Mormon spends five verses on the method.

chapter.title: Mormon twice steps out of the narrative
chapter.text: Verses 13 through 17 describe his sources, and verses 27 through 30 draw a doctrinal lesson. Both asides are marked and then closed.

chapter.title: The abridgment names its own scale
chapter.text: Verse 13 states what exists, "many records kept of the proceedings of this people, by many of this people, which are particular and very large." Verse 14 states what fits, "a hundredth part of the proceedings of this people... cannot be contained in this work," and lists nine categories it is leaving out, from wars and contentions to "their shipping and their building of ships." Verse 15 adds "many books and many records of every kind." The reader is told the size of the library, the size of the excerpt, and the categories dropped, all inside three verses.

chapter.title: Peace and the combinations coexist
chapter.text: Verse 23 says the years of continual peace are also the years the secret combinations grow, hidden in the settled parts. The safety and the danger are the same years.

chapter.title: Ignorance is given as the reason they survived
chapter.text: The heads of government did not know, so nothing was done. Mormon states the cause without assigning blame.

chapter.title: Growth and pride arrive together
chapter.text: Tens of thousands are baptized in verse 26, and pride enters the church in verse 33. Seven verses separate the two reports.

chapter.title: Persecution refines the humble part
chapter.text: Verses 34 and 35 have the humbler people suffering and then growing stronger, firmer, and sanctified. The chapter's last word on them is yielded hearts.

applications.title: Check whether the name still fits
applications.text: The land kept the name desolate because of a destruction long past, though no part of it was actually desolate except for timber. Labels outlive the conditions that produced them, so ask now and then what a name is still describing.

applications.title: Build with what the place gives you
applications.text: No timber, so they learned cement. Constraints are usually an instruction about method rather than a verdict on the project.

applications.title: Plant for the timber you will not cut
applications.text: They let trees grow so that later generations could build. Some work only pays out to people you will not meet.

applications.title: Say how much you had to leave out
applications.text: Mormon told the reader his account is a hundredth part. Naming the scope of what you are summarizing keeps your summary honest.

applications.title: Look for what grows during the peaceful years
applications.text: The combinations spread while the land was quiet and nobody was looking. Calm is when unattended things get established.

applications.title: Let the result outrun your expectation
applications.text: The high priests and the teachers were themselves astonished beyond measure at how the church was growing. When something goes better than you planned for, say so plainly instead of writing yourself back in as the cause.

applications.title: Locate the pride precisely
applications.text: Mormon corrects himself mid-sentence: the pride entered the hearts of people who professed to belong, and he will not let the phrase land on the church itself. When something goes wrong in an institution, name the people it went wrong in, since an abstraction cannot repent.

applications.title: Affliction can go either way
applications.text: The humbler part of the people fasted and prayed often under persecution and grew firmer in the faith of Christ. Pressure sanctifies nobody by itself, and what this verse credits is what they did while they were under it.

questions.text: What small thing am I calling little that is growing?
What have I moved away from rather than settled?
What am I doing now that only pays off after me?
What am I leaving out of the account I give of myself?
What is established in my life that I have not looked at?
Where has pride entered, and would I locate it in myself or in the institution?
What has affliction made firmer in me?
